chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Hiring Roy Eldridge on his playing, not the Stampede solo story
summary: Horace denies that he hired Roy for copying Hawkins' Stampede solo; he hired him for his fast, correct playing on tunes like 'I Got Rhythm'.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Okay, well, that's good to clear that up. I'm sure that'll be helpful. Here's another one. Let's see. You know, we were talking about when you hired Roy Eldridge? And let's see -- this -- you hired him in Pittsburgh, and that was about that same time, 1928, I guess.

Yes, and it says he brought in Roy, and you let Sprat go, and Syd Valentine usually alternated between first, or melody lead, and second trumpet parts, specialty solos, such as growl or muted, while Roy played the hot solos, third chair. Now it says here, "Roy has recalled that he was hired on the strength of his playing Coleman Hawkins' chorus off the record 'Stampede,' on his horn." This
a quote from Metronome magazine. Do you remember Metronome, the --
-- jazz magazine? Roy stated that in 1946, that he played that particular, probably was a copied solo that he got off a record.
Well, I didn't highroll on the strength of that. I hired Roy on the strength of what Roy could played.

He might have just had that up his sleeve to play, but it was no big thing made out of it. I hired Roy because the thing that, as I said before, actually sold me on Roy, he could play fast tunes like I Got Rhythm and played the correct things and this is why I hired Roy. Where this information came from, I don't know.
Speakin'. May I inject something here for someone to know?
